results.problem: Disk active set complexity for 2D geographic disks
results.quote: The family $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D})=\{\mathcal{A}(c):c=(g,r),g\in\mathbb{S}^2,r\ge 0\}$ of distinct disk active sets satisfies $|\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D})|\le\sum_{i=0}^4\genfrac(){pt}{2}{n}{i}=O(n^4)$, and reaches $|\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{D})|=\Omega(n^2)$ on worst-case n-object collections.

results.problem: Contiguous ordering of 2D disk active sets
results.bound: No linear order makes $\mathcal{A}(c)$ contiguous for all disks $c$ (even for 3 objects)
results.quote: Place three objects $V=\{1,2,3\}$ at the vertices of a small equilateral spherical triangle on $\mathbb{S}^2$. A disk centered at the midpoint of any pair $\{i,j\}$ with radius $\Delta(s_i,s_j)/2$ admits only $\{i,j\}$; because the first and last elements in any permutation of $V$ are non-contiguous, no linear order makes $\mathcal{A}(c)$ contiguous for all disks $c$.

results.quote: For any graph $G=(V,E)$ of row width $B$, disk $c$, and budget $\ell\ge 1$: ... (c) for $|\mathcal{A}(c)|\ge 2$, $\mathcal{H}_\ell(c)$ is strongly connected if and only if $\ell\ge\ell_{\mathrm{SC}}(c)$, where the cut rank is $\ell_{\mathrm{SC}}(c)=\mathrm{max}_{\varnothing\neq S\subseteq\mathcal{A}(c)}\mathrm{min}_{u\in S,v\in C_u(c)\backslash S}\mathrm{rank}_{u,c}(v)$ (with inner minimum $\infty$ if no edge of $\mathcal{H}_\infty(c)$ leaves $S$).

For every disk $c=(g,r)$ and coordinate $z$, $F(z)\cap\mathcal{A}(c)\neq\emptyset\Longleftrightarrow F(z)\subseteq\mathcal{A}(c)$. Because all $v\in F(z)$ have the same distance $\Delta(z,g)$ to $g$, a disk never splits a fiber (Figure 2(a)), and the induced fiber subgraph $G[F(z)]$ is identical under every disk that admits $z$.

results.problem: Strong connectivity decomposition of active projection
results.bound: $G[\mathcal{A}(c)]$ is strongly connected if intra-fiber connectivity and coordinate-quotient connectivity hold
results.quote: For any directed graph $G=(V,E)$ and disk $c$, $G[\mathcal{A}(c)]$ is strongly connected if: (i) (Intra-fiber connectivity) $G[F(z)]$ is strongly connected for every active fiber $F(z)\subseteq\mathcal{A}(c)$; and (ii) (Coordinate-quotient connectivity) the quotient graph formed by contracting each active fiber $F(z)\subseteq\mathcal{A}(c)$ into a single site vertex $z$ is strongly connected.

results.bound: $B_g\ge a_\alpha(h_c+1)=\Theta(\log^2(nM/\delta))$, $K_f\ge C_f\log(3nM/\delta)$ guarantees $\mathcal{H}_\infty(c)=G[\mathcal{A}(c)]$ strongly connected with probability $\ge 1-\delta$
results.quote: Under the regular marked-site model (Appendix A.4), for any disk $c$ with $M\pi_c\ge \log(6/\delta)$, setting quotas $B_g\ge a_\alpha(h_c+1)=\Theta(\log^2(nM/\delta))$, $K_f\ge C_f\log(3nM/\delta)$ guarantees that: ... results.problem: Greedy routing and approximation on compact disks
results.bound: Greedy routing reaches $v$ in at most $\lceil \log_\alpha(D_x/\varepsilon_\alpha)\rceil$ hops; local minimum satisfies $d(x_q,x_u)\le\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha-1}\min_{v\in\mathcal{A}(c)}d(x_q,x_v)$
results.quote: On the event of Theorem 3.7, if $\mathrm{diam}(\Omega_c)\le\rho_c$ and $K_f\ge|F(z)|-1$ for $F(z)\subseteq\mathcal{A}(c)$, then for every $u,v\in\mathcal{A}(c)$ with $d(x_u,x_v)>\varepsilon_\alpha$, $u$ has an active out-neighbor $w\in F(s_v)$ satisfying $d(x_w,x_v)\le d(x_u,x_v)/\alpha$. Greedy routing therefore reaches $v$ in at most $\lceil \log_\alpha(D_x/\varepsilon_\alpha)\rceil$ hops, and any local minimum $u$ for query $x_q$ satisfies $d(x_q,x_u)\le\frac{\alpha+1}{\alpha-1}\min_{v\in\mathcal{A}(c)}d(x_q,x_v)$.

results.bound: $\mathrm{row}(u)$ contains at most $B$ valid IDs ordered by $\prec_u$ ($4nB$ bytes in total); witness and coverage guarantees
results.quote: For $B_v+B_g\le B$, Algorithm 1 guarantees that: (i) every candidate $v\in F(z)\backslash\{u\}$ examined in lines 7-11 is either stored in $\mathrm{row}(u)$ or witnessed by some $w\in\mathrm{row}(u)\cap F(z)$ with $d(x_v,x_w)\le d(x_u,x_v)/\alpha$; (ii) if $L_u(\rho)\le B_g$, every site $z\neq s_u$ with $\Delta(s_u,z)\le\rho$ has $\mathrm{row}(u)\cap F(z)\neq\varnothing$; and (iii) $\mathrm{row}(u)$ contains at most $B$ valid IDs ordered by $\prec_u$ ($4nB$ bytes in total).

results.problem: Fixed-width row construction for REACH index
results.bound: Algorithm 1 constructs one width-$B$ row per vertex by merging global vector candidates with a fiber-aware geographic stream
results.quote: Offline, each vertex merges globally closest vector candidates with a nearest-first geographic stream into one row; online, beam search evaluates vector distances only for the first $\ell$ active entries of each visited row.

results.problem: Two-phase first-$\ell$-active expansion for query processing
results.bound: Beam search traverses $\mathcal{H}_\ell(c_q)$ with at most $\min\{\ell,B\}$ vector evaluations per expanded vertex
results.quote: In Phase 1 (Lines 1-7), the algorithm scans $\mathrm{row}(u)$ sequentially, testing each neighbor $v$ against disk $c_q$ ... the scan stops once $j=\ell$. In Phase 2 (Lines 8-10), $D$-dimensional Euclidean distances $d(x_q,x_v)$ are computed only for $v\in A$ (at most $\min\{\ell,B\}$ vector evaluations vs. at most $B$ scalar checks in Phase 1).

results.bound: $O(n)$ grid directory collects $\tau=16$ active seeds in $1.2\mu\mathrm{s}$ using $<0.4\%$ of graph memory
results.quote: To seed the beam, a $0.5^\circ\times 0.5^\circ$ grid directory [14, 34] scans Chebyshev rings around $g_q$ to collect $\tau=16$ active seeds in $1.2\mu\mathrm{s}$ using $<0.4\%$ of graph memory (Appendix B.2; graph-descent seeding is compared in Exp-5).
